name: Increasing by Modulo
description: Toad Zitz has an array of integers, each integer is between $$$0$$$ and $$$m-1$$$ inclusive. The integers are $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$. In one operation Zitz can choose an integer $$$k$$$ and $$$k$$$ indices $$$i_1, i_2, \ldots, i_k$$$ such that $$$1 \leq i_1 \lt i_2 \lt \ldots \lt i_k \leq n$$$. He should then change $$$a_{i_j}$$$ to $$$((a_{i_j}+1) \bmod m)$$$ for each chosen integer $$$i_j$$$. The integer $$$m$$$ is fixed for all operations and indices. Here $$$x \bmod y$$$ denotes the remainder of the division of $$$x$$$ by $$$y$$$. Zitz wants to make his array non-decreasing with the minimum number of such operations. Find this minimum number of operations.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \leq n, m \leq 300\,000$$$) — the number of integers in the array and the parameter $$$m$$$. The next line contains $$$n$$$ space-separated integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \leq a_i \lt m$$$) — the given array.
output_specification: Output one integer: the minimum number of described operations Zitz needs to make his array non-decreasing. If no operations required, print $$$0$$$. It is easy to see that with enough operations Zitz can always make his array non-decreasing.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1168A — Increasing by Modulo [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
